_about: Demand (PRD, "Four demand bars" and "Pacing"). Set by M3-01 and given its ratios by M3-06. Every value here is a starting value with no source behind it, to tune in M3-21. Each bar runs from -100 to 100 and is the sum of its parts, one per input. Each input is a ratio of running totals from 0 up, and each weight is the bar points one whole unit of its input is worth: an input that raises the bar has a weight of 0 or more, and one that lowers it 0 or less. Residential reads open jobs and unemployed workers, each per worker. Commercial reads spending power (residents weighted by `spendingByWealth`): the shop jobs that spending keeps busy, `shopJobsPerSpending` to a unit of it and at most one per worker, less the shop jobs there are, per shop job it keeps busy; then workers without a job, per worker; then shop jobs beyond what the spending keeps busy, per shop job. Office reads medium and high education workers without an office job, per worker, and the office jobs residents and businesses would buy, `officeJobsPerBuyer` to each resident and each shop or factory job, less the office jobs there are, per office job they would buy. Industrial reads unemployed low and medium education workers, per worker; the factory jobs shops need goods from, `factoryJobsPerShopJob` to a shop job, less the factory jobs there are, per factory job they need; and open office jobs, per worker, which lower it so a dense city leans on offices. Industrial reads nothing above 0 while no road the player built reaches an outside connection. A bar whose parts add up to more than 100 either way has them scaled down together. `dailyShare` is how far each part moves toward its new value each game day, so bars do not flicker. `outsidePull` adds `bar` to the residential bar's target while the city has never had `untilResidents` residents, and again whenever it has nobody, so the first houses always come (M3-06). Since #361 it is added to the other parts and is not a floor under them, so a town with no jobs falls below zero and empties; its first newcomers are not counted as unemployed for `newcomer.graceDays` in pops.json, so it still starts. `buildingsPerDayAtFullDemand` is, for each zone, how many buildings the grower adds a game day with its bar at 100 (M3-07): a zone builds only while its bar is above zero, at its rate times the bar over 100, at least one, times its development charge's share from economy.json (M4-08), so a bar barely above zero still builds one a day with no charge; the whole part is built over the day and the fraction left over is one more building with that chance, drawn on the day's last tick. Until M4-08 the figure was rounded up. Mixed has no bar and reads the lower of residential and commercial. Starting values to tune in M3-21: on an empty city a 192 m street zoned R1 six deep on both sides fills in about a game week, while the residential bar climbs toward the outside pull's 25. `arrivalsPerYearAtFullDemand` is the least number of residents who move in a game year with the residential bar at 100: 17,000 in M3-08, 40,000 since M3-21 (#192); fewer come as the bar falls, and none while it is at or below zero. Since M3-21 more come where there is room for them: with the bar at b, a day brings at least ceil(b / 100 x empty room / `fillDays`) people, the empty room in homes newcomers can reach, so towers fill in about `fillDays` game days and a street of houses at the floor's pace (PRD "Pacing"). `unfilledHomesMax` holds new homes back while that many homes newcomers can reach, or more, are still filling: room left for a household, and fewer people than `homeFullShare` of their room. So free room fills before more is built, a few towers fill side by side, and a tower a death has left a few places short does not count (M3-08, a count since M3-21, PRD "Turnover"). Since #426, as #420 proposed, a bigger city may fill more at once: the most is the larger of `unfilledHomesMax` and one home for every `residentsPerUnfilledHome` residents, 20 homes at 200,000. `openJobsShareMax` does the same for workplaces (M3-09): the grower adds no building to a zone that offers jobs while the open jobs in that zone's buildings, counting those on a road that reaches an outside connection, are more than that share of their jobs and more than `openJobsMin`, so a zone starting again from nothing is not held by its first workshop (M3-21). Each bar shows what is waiting (#420): a last part, `homesFilling` on residential and `jobsOpen` on the others, takes away the share of what the other parts add above zero that the homes still filling, or the zone's open jobs, make up of the most the grower allows before it holds the zone back, so a bar reads 0 while the grower waits for room or jobs to fill. It never takes a bar below zero and has no weight here. `jobMatching` weights the workplaces a pop looking for work draws among (M3-09, PRD "Job matching"): each open job its education allows counts 1 / (1 + (t / `halfWeightSeconds`)^`falloffPower`), t the free-flow seconds from the pop's home, so a job `halfWeightSeconds` away counts half as much as one next door, and a larger whole `falloffPower` makes the weight fall away faster beyond that. Residential also reads its residents' average satisfaction, weighted by pop size, less `satisfactionNeutral`, over 100 (M3-10): residents happier than that raise the bar and unhappier ones lower it, and a city with no residents reads 0. `departuresPerYearAtFullDemand` is how many residents leave a game year with the residential bar at -100, the least satisfied first; fewer go as the bar rises, and none while it is at or above zero (M3-10, PRD "Satisfaction"). `vacancy` sets when a building that people have left stands vacant and then abandoned (M3-24, PRD "Vacancy and abandonment"): a home with nobody in it, or a workplace with none of its jobs filled while its zone's bar is below zero, is vacant once it has stood `newDays` game days since it was built or came back into use, and a building vacant for `abandonDays` game days is abandoned. An abandoned building offers no room and no jobs until its zone's bar is above zero again. `redevelopment` paces redevelopment (M3-14, PRD "Rezoning"): once a game day the owner of a building whose ground is zoned up to a higher density of its zone, with the zone's bar above zero, considers rebuilding with a chance of `chancePerDay` times its land value less `valueFrom` over 100 less `valueFrom`, at least 0, times the bar over 100, so owners on better ground and in hotter demand rebuild sooner. At most `perDayMax` buildings a game day are replaced, every one a new building takes in counted, spread over the day's ticks, or cleared where an abandoned one stands on ground zoned for something else, so a rezoned district changes over months and not in a day. No prices here, so no source years.
